info.title: CinemaGo users service
info.description:
Users service of CinemaGo. Handles accounts, login with JWT access tokens and refresh tokens, roles, and the token check that the Traefik gateway runs before every protected request.

## How to log in

1. `POST /users/register` with name, email and password (or use the admin from ADMIN_EMAIL and ADMIN_PASSWORD).
2. `POST /users/login` returns `token` (access token, valid ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES, default 15) and `refreshToken` (valid 7 days, works once).
3. Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on protected calls (use the Authorize button).
4. When the access token expires, `POST /users/refresh` with the refresh token gives new tokens.

Logout (`DELETE /users/{id}/sessions`), a password change and deleting the user make all older tokens stop working.

## Gateway

Through Traefik (server `/api`, for example `http://localhost:8080/api/users/login`) register, login and refresh are public, everything else needs a token. For other services Traefik calls `GET /auth/verify` and passes `X-User-Id` and `X-User-Role` on.

## Roles

`user` can read and change only their own account. `admin` can list all users, change roles and change or delete any user. There is always at least one admin: the last admin cannot be deleted or made a user.

## Rate limit

Register, login and refresh allow RATE_LIMIT_REQUESTS calls (default 10) per client IP and path in RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS (default 60). After that they answer 429 with a `Retry-After` header in seconds.

## Validation

Name 1 to 100 characters (not only spaces), a valid email (saved in lowercase, unique), password 6 to 128 characters. Broken rules return 400 like `{"error": "email: must be a valid email"}`.

## Errors

Every error from this service is JSON like `{"error": "user not found"}`. This includes bad JSON bodies (400, 415, 422), bad path or query values (400) and unknown paths (404). When the service is down, the gateway itself answers 502 or 503 without a JSON body.

servers.description: Direct to the users service (dev port 8081)

get.description:
Traefik ForwardAuth calls this before every protected request through the gateway. When the bearer token is valid it answers 200 with the X-User-Id and X-User-Role headers, which Traefik copies to the target service. Otherwise it answers 401 and Traefik returns that 401 to the client.

The token is checked for signature, expiry, an existing user and the current token version (logout and password change make old tokens invalid). Not routed through the gateway, it is only called inside docker.

X-User-Id.description: Id of the logged in user, for example 7

401.description: The bearer token is missing, expired, invalid, or was logged out (logout, password change and deleting the user make old tokens stop working).

500.description: Unexpected database error. The details are only in the service log.

get.description: Returns `{"status":"ok"}` when the service is running. No token needed. Docker and Traefik use it to know when the service is ready.

Returns one page of all users, sorted by id.

**Who can call it:** admins only. Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from login.

400.description: `page` or `pageSize` is out of range or not a number.

value.error: Failed to deserialize query string: page: invalid digit found in string

Out of range.summary: page below 1 or pageSize not 1 to 100

value.error: page must be at least 1 and pageSize 1 to 100

401.description: The bearer token is missing, expired, invalid, or was logged out (logout, password change and deleting the user make old tokens stop working).

403.description: You are logged in but not an admin.

500.description: Unexpected database error. The details are only in the service log.

post.description:
Checks email and password and returns an access token, a refresh token and the user. No token needed (public through the gateway).

The access token is a JWT valid for ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES (default 15). Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on protected calls. The refresh token is valid 7 days and works once, use it with POST /users/refresh.

**Rate limit:** RATE_LIMIT_REQUESTS calls per IP in RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS (default 10 per 60 seconds), then 429 with a Retry-After header. Behind Traefik the IP is the last address in X-Forwarded-For.

400.description: The body is not valid JSON.

example.error: Failed to parse the request body as JSON: key must be a string at line 1 column 2

401.description: No account with this email, or the password is wrong. Both give the same message on purpose.

415.description: The body is not sent as JSON (missing `Content-Type: application/json`).

422.description: The JSON is valid but a field is missing or has the wrong type.

example.error: Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: missing field `password` at line 1 column 2

429.description: Rate limit: more than RATE_LIMIT_REQUESTS calls (default 10) from the same IP to this path in RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS (default 60). Wait the number of seconds in Retry-After.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before the next try

example.error: too many requests, try again later

500.description: Unexpected database error. The details are only in the service log.

**Who can call it:** any logged in user. Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from login.

Same as PUT /users/{id} with your own id, without needing to know it.

**Who can call it:** any logged in user. Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from login.

**Rules:** name 1 to 100 characters (not only spaces), a valid email that no other account uses. The email is saved in lowercase.

put.description:
Changes the password of the logged in user. The old password must be correct and the new one must have 6 to 128 characters.

After the change all refresh tokens are deleted and old access tokens stop working, so log in again with the new password.

**Who can call it:** any logged in user, only for their own account. Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from login.

401.description: The token is missing or invalid, or the old password is wrong.

post.summary: Get new tokens with a refresh token
post.description:
Trades a refresh token for a new access token and a new refresh token. No access token needed (public through the gateway).

Each refresh token works only once: after this call the old one is deleted. Refresh tokens are valid 7 days and are removed on logout, password change and when the user is deleted.

**Rate limit:** RATE_LIMIT_REQUESTS calls per IP in RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS (default 10 per 60 seconds), then 429 with a Retry-After header. Behind Traefik the IP is the last address in X-Forwarded-For.

requestBody.description: The refresh token from login or from the last refresh.

200.description: New tokens, the old refresh token stops working.

post.description:
Creates a new user. No token needed (public through the gateway).

**Rules:** name 1 to 100 characters (not only spaces), a valid email that is not used yet (saved in lowercase), password 6 to 128 characters. The very first user becomes `admin` when no admin was created from ADMIN_EMAIL, everyone else gets `user`.

After register the service sends a welcome message to the notifications service. If notifications is down, register still works.

**Rate limit:** RATE_LIMIT_REQUESTS calls per IP in RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS (default 10 per 60 seconds), then 429 with a Retry-After header. Behind Traefik the IP is the last address in X-Forwarded-For.

Returns one user by id. Read from the Valkey cache when possible.

**Who can call it:** inside docker every service can call it without a token (`http://users:8080/users/{id}`), for example to check that a user exists. Through the gateway (`/api/users/{id}`) any logged in user can call it with a bearer token.

delete.description:
Deletes the account and its refresh tokens. Old access tokens of this user stop working.

**Who can call it:** the user themselves, or an admin for any user. Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from login.

The last admin cannot be deleted.

put.summary: Change the role of a user
put.description:
Makes a user an `admin` or a normal `user`. The new role is in tokens issued after this call, old tokens still have the old role until they expire.

**Who can call it:** admins only. Send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from login.

**Rules:** the role must be `user` or `admin`. The last admin cannot be made a normal user, there is always at least one admin.
